summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for her seventh cycle of high-dose methotrexate for diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with CNS involvement. Due to recent high ostomy output and hypomagnesemia, she was initially hydrated with IV fluids and given IV magnesium replacement. Chemotherapy was delayed by one day due to worsening neutropenia, but proceeded when counts stabilized. Methotrexate was administered at 3.5 g/m² and well tolerated. Leucovorin rescue was started 24 hours post-infusion, and methotrexate levels declined appropriately, falling below 0.05 before discharge. Stool studies were negative for infection. Her diabetes was managed by holding metformin during admission, and she was discharged home with medication adjustments, including a revised metformin dose and new magnesium supplementation, along with three doses of oral leucovorin.
